name: AI support desk · Triage, specialists and a judge

parameters.content:
## AI support desk · Triage, specialists and a judge
A triage agent routes each Zendesk ticket to a specialist agent that can read Shopify, Stripe or the knowledge base. A separate judge checks every answer before it is sent, refunds are decided by a written policy in code, and anything uncertain reaches a person with the facts already gathered.

**Platforms:** Zendesk, OpenAI, Claude, Shopify, Supabase, Stripe, Pinecone, Slack, Typeform
**Source and tests:** github.com/kimjoshuadr/n8n-workflows · `systems/ai-support-desk`

## 1. Intake and triage
Zendesk in. One agent reads the ticket; code decides what always goes to a person.

nodes.name: Section: Specialists, each with its own tools

parameters.content:
## 2. Specialists, each with its own tools
Orders reads Shopify, billing reads Stripe, technical and general search the knowledge base in Pinecone.

## 3. Refund policy, in code
An agent can ask for a refund. Only this section can make one.

options.systemMessage: You are the Triage agent on a support desk. Read the ticket and decide: topic ('orders' for delivery, order status and returns; 'billing' for charges, invoices and refunds; 'technical' for something not working; 'other' for anything else), urgency ('low', 'normal' or 'high'), sentiment ('calm', 'frustrated' or 'angry') and the language it is written in as a two-letter code. Do not answer the ticket.

options.systemMessage: You are the Orders agent. Look the order up in Shopify before saying anything about it. Reply in under 140 words, plain text, signed 'The Acme support team'. State only what a tool returned. If a tool returned nothing useful, set needs_human true and confidence low instead of guessing. Never promise a refund, a date or a discount: describe what you found and what happens next.

nodes.name: Add the refund to the reply

parameters.jsCode:
const a = $("Inside the policy?").first().json;
return [{ json: { ...a, reply: a.reply + "\n\nWe have refunded " + a.refund.amount.toFixed(2) + " to your original payment method. It usually arrives within 5 to 10 working days.", refunded: true } }];

parameters.text: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ticket: { subject: $json.subject, body: $json.body }, reply: $json.reply, facts: $json.facts }) }}

options.systemMessage: You are the Judge agent. You did not write this reply. Pass it only if every statement in it is supported by the listed facts, it answers what the customer asked, it promises nothing, and the tone is calm and plain. List every problem you find.

parameters.jsCode:
const h = $("Write the handover").first().json;
return [{ json: { channel: "#support", level: h.urgency === "high" ? "critical" : "warn", text: "Ticket #" + h.ticket_id + " (" + h.topic + ") needs a person: " + h.reasons.join("; ") + "." } }];

const before = $("Measure against the SLA").all();
return $input.all().map((_, i) => { const t = before[i].json; return { json: { channel: "#support", level: t.stage === "breached" ? "critical" : "warn", text: t.stage === "breached" ? "Response time missed on #" + t.id + ": waited " + t.waited + " min (limit " + t.limit + ")." : "Response time at risk on #" + t.id + ": " + (t.limit - t.waited) + " min left." } }; });

options.systemMessage: You are the Auditor agent. Grade a support reply that has already been sent, from 1 to 5: was it correct for the question, complete, and honest about what it did not know? Name the single most important thing to fix, or 'nothing'.

parameters.jsCode:
const rows = $input.all().map((i) => i.json).filter((r) => r.question);
return [{ json: { count: rows.length, questions: rows.slice(0, 80).map((r) => "- [" + r.topic + "] " + String(r.question).slice(0, 160) + " (" + (r.reasons ?? []).join(", ") + ")").join("\n") } }];

options.systemMessage: You are the Gaps agent. Group these tickets the agents could not answer into at most five themes. For each, give the theme, how many tickets, and the one change that would let an agent answer next time: a help article to write, a tool to add, or a policy to clarify. Plain text, no preamble.

parameters.text: ={{ ':books: ' + $('Gather the questions').first().json.count + ' tickets went to a person last week.\n' + ($json.output ?? $('Gather the questions').first().json.questions) }}
={{ ':white_check_mark: The agents answered every ticket they were given last week.' }}

options.systemMessage: You are the Recovery agent. A customer rated their support 1 or 2 out of 5. Draft a short, personal note a human support lead could send: acknowledge what went wrong in their words, do not make excuses, do not offer compensation, and ask one question that would help put it right. Under 90 words. This is a draft for a person, never sent by you.

parameters.jsCode:
const s = $("Read the survey").first().json;
return [{ json: { channel: "#support", level: "warn", text: s.email + " rated ticket #" + s.ticket_id + " " + s.score + "/5" + (s.comment ? ": \"" + s.comment.slice(0, 200) + "\"" : "") + ". A follow-up ticket is open with a draft reply." } }];
